stem: Which of the following describes all solutions to the inequality \(7 - 3x > 22\)?
solution: Divide both sides by \(-3\) and reverse the inequality sign: \(x < -5\).
Check: \(x = -6\) gives \(7 + 18 = 25 > 22\), while \(x = 0\) gives \(7\), which is not greater than 22.

explanation.A: Incorrect. Dividing by the negative number \(-3\) reverses the inequality sign; this answer keeps the sign unchanged.
explanation.B: Correct. \(-3x > 15\), and dividing by \(-3\) reverses the sign: \(x < -5\).
explanation.C: Incorrect. \(x = 0\) is less than 5 but gives \(7 - 0 = 7\), not greater than 22. This drops the negative sign when dividing.
explanation.D: Incorrect. This adds 7 to 22 instead of subtracting it, giving \(-3x > 29\).

verify:
P = lambda s: value(s.replace('\\le', '<=').replace('\\ge', '>='))
x = symbols('x')
s = solve_univariate_inequality(7 - 3*x > 22, x, relational=False)
assert s == Interval.open(-oo, -5)
assert solve_univariate_inequality(P(choices[answer]), x, relational=False) == s
assert all(solve_univariate_inequality(P(choices[k]), x, relational=False) != s for k in choices if k != answer)
